messages:
emily_oncall: Paging: alerting on elevated 5xx from prod-gateway starting ~09:12 UTC. Large spike in TLS handshake failures (525/ssl-handshake + timeouts). Customer-facing 502/504 reports. Observability: 5xx went from ~0.02% to 2.3%. Paging SREs now, tagging @incident-bot for SEV2 escalation.

incident-bot: :rotating_light: Incident created: INCIDENT-2024-1719001234 (SEV2). Pages sent to on-call rotation and sec-sre. Incident channel: #incidents/1719001234 (this thread). Please acknowledge.

raj: oncall ack, I'm on it. emily, can you paste a sample gateway log or error trace?

emily_oncall: here’s a log snippet from the gateway at 09:13:
```
2026-03-15T09:13:22Z gateway[proxy-12]: tls: handshake failure from 10.12.8.45: tls: failed to verify certificate: x509: certificate has expired or is not yet valid
2026-03-15T09:13:22Z gateway[proxy-12]: upstream request failed: code=525, msg="SSL handshake failed"
```
Affected zones: prod-gateway-us-west and prod-gateway-eu. Error rate correlates with traffic spikes to those clusters.

dana: pulled cert metadata from secret-store: leaf cert for prod-gateway expired 2026-03-14T23:58:00Z. Rotator didn't replace it. I'm tailing the rotator logs now.

cleo: Support reporting 3 enterprise customers complaining about 502/504s, some have retries failing. Drafting status page message and notifying account teams. :warning:

raj: ok mitigation options off the top: 1) failover traffic to backup gateway pool that has older working chain 2) roll-forward rotator fix (if quick) 3) scoped temporary relax of mTLS enforcement for partner clients. Which is quickest?

dana: backup pool currently has an older chain installed and should accept connections. I can shift small percentage to backup while we fix rotator. Rotator logs show KMS decrypt errors when fetching new private key.

raj: let's do gradual traffic steering to backup. I'll start 10% -> 50% -> 100% rollback plan. Also restarting rotator pod after we attempt manual decrypt.

emily_oncall: actioning routing now. Updating incident timeline and assigning roles.

raj: executing first step. Patching traffic steer:
```
# quick weighted shift (pseudo)
kubectl annotate svc/prod-gateway infra.redwood.io/traffic-steer=backup=10 --overwrite -n prod
# or use ingress weight API
```
Switching 10% to prod-gateway-backup. Watching 5xx.

incident-bot: Update: 10% traffic steered to backup pool. 5xx dropped from 2.3% -> 1.1%. Continuing.

morgan_sec: caution: if we disable mTLS enforcement broadly we risk customer trust. Recommend scoped exception by client certificate thumbprint or IP CIDR for known partner customers. I can craft an envoy filter to skip mTLS for specific SANs.

raj: noted. At 50% shift now. Restarting cert-rotator: `kubectl rollout restart deploy/cert-rotator -n infra`. Watching logs.

incident-bot: Pager update: traffic at 50% to backup; 5xx now ~0.25% and trending down.

support_team: CS update: notifying top impacted customers, message draft in #support-drafts for approval. ETA 15m.

dana: rotator logs show KMS decrypt failure: `error: crypto/decrypt: permission denied` referencing KMS key version that rotated 2026-03-14T00:05Z. Looks like KMS key policy change prevented the rotator service account from decrypting the new private key. Opening infra-kms ticket.

morgan_sec: Can infra temporarily allow the previous key version for rotator to decrypt? If not, we should provision a manual cert push while KMS is fixed and then revert. I'll prepare an envoy filter patch to whitelist partner cert thumbprints in case we need it.

raj: traffic at 100% to backup now as a precaution. Health checks green on backup pool, 5xx baseline back to normal (<0.1%). Preparing plan to manually inject a valid cert into main cluster if rotator can't decrypt.

incident-bot: Update: cert-rotator restart failed -> CrashLoopBackOff. Investigating daemon logs.

dana: because rotator can't decrypt, restart doesn't help. Performing manual cert push to secret-store and reloading gateway config on both primary and backup. Manual steps:
```
# upload cert bundle to secret-store
gcloud secrets versions add prod-gateway-cert --data-file=cert_bundle.pem --project=redwood-prod
# reload gateway
kubectl rollout restart deploy/prod-gateway -n prod
```
Quick curl test after manual push: `curl -v --resolve prod-gateway.example.com:443:10.1.2.3 https://prod-gateway.example.com/health` returns 200 and shows cert valid to 2027-04-01.

raj: after manual push, 5xx back down to ~0.05%. I'm starting gradual shift back to primary (10% increments) and monitoring.

emily_oncall: handoff coming up at 10:45 UTC. Summary for next on-call: root cause = leaf cert expired due to cert-rotator failing to decrypt new key (KMS permission change). Immediate mitigation = failover to backup pool + manual cert push to main. Action items:
- dana: continue rotator/KMS investigation and own infra-kms ticket OPEN-345
- raj: own traffic steering and postmortem timeline
- morgan_sec: scope and document any temporary mTLS whitelist used, evaluate security postop reductions
- cleo: finalize status page and customer comms (cc @carlos_pm)

carlos_pm: acknowledged. coordinating customer comms now; will update stakeholders.

alex_night: taking handoff, oncall ack. Noted incident state and actions. Starting 2hr monitoring window. Postmortem owner: raj.

cleo: status page updated and sent. Customers notified. Incident marked: SEV2 -> mitigated. Will open postmortem doc with timeline + follow-ups (rotator hardening, KMS permission guardrails).

incident-bot: Incident update: mitigated at 10:34 UTC. Root cause: rotator KMS permission change prevented cert rotation -> expired leaf cert -> TLS handshake failures. Next steps: postmortem + infra KMS ACL review.

emily_oncall: thanks team. leaving notes in playbook and adding follow-ups for automated alerting on cert expiry window and rotator decryption errors. Closing handoff. :white_check_mark:
